recommendation: Keep the audit commit as-is. No core follow-up is needed for FHIR-26937 unless a future work-group decision changes primitive JSON serialization rules.
issue_request: FHIR-26937 was a Published FHIR-I R5 change request, resolved Persuasive with Modification, asking the JSON representation of primitive elements to cover the newer integer-related primitive types and to clarify that the 64-bit integer type is not serialized as a JSON number.
initial_application: The historical implementation commit acc7cdb646 changed source/json.html to list unsignedInt and positiveInt with integer and decimal as JSON-number primitives, and to call out integer64 among the string-serialized primitive types. A later cleanup commit, 8592e12072, only changed spelling from "data type" to "datatype" and did not alter the serialization rule.
additional_context: source/datatypes.html independently says integer64 is a JSON String while unsignedInt and positiveInt are JSON numbers. FHIR-I minutes from 2020-04-27 record the FHIR-26937 9-0-0 vote as adding a new integer type that is not a JSON number but a string. A later implementers Zulip thread and FHIR-28586 clarified that unsignedInt and positiveInt were not intended to serialize as strings. FHIR-39841 later reinforced the same distinction when the submitter accepted that integer64 differs from other number datatypes in JSON.
reconciliation: Published an empty no-change audit commit because the current core source already implements the issue's final intent and related clarifications. No source files were changed.

related_jiras.note: Follow-up from the Zulip confusion around FHIR-26937; it confirmed unsignedInt and positiveInt value types should be System.Integer, not System.String, and was already represented on the combined branch.
Later Resolved - No Change request whose submitter accepted that integer64 has a different JSON representation from other number datatypes.
